title: Frobenius basis span of a compositum
statement: Let $p$ be prime, $K$ and $L$ fields of characteristic $p$, and $L/K$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] with a finite $K$-basis $(e_i)_{i<n}$. Let $S$ be a subfield of $K$ containing $K^p=\{a^p:a\in K\}$. The subfield of $L$ generated by $L^p=\{y^p:y\in L\}$ and the image of $S$ is exactly $\{\sum_{i<n}a_i e_i^p:a_i\in S\}$. Coefficients in $K$ are mapped to $L$ by the extension embedding. No linear independence of $(e_i^p)$ over $S$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 07P4 (lemma-intersection-subfields), proof of (2), the two displayed coefficient presentations; arbitrary finite bases in place of power bases

proof.text: Put b_i=e_i^p. For y in L, expand y=sum c_i e_i in the supplied finite basis. The Frobenius sum and product identities give y^p=sum c_i^p b_i. Conversely, if a_i is in K^p, write a_i=c_i^p; then sum a_i b_i=(sum c_i e_i)^p. Hence L^p is exactly the K^p-span of b. In particular it contains 1 and b_i b_j, so those elements have K^p-coefficient expansions.

source.place: Tag 07P4 (lemma-intersection-subfields), proof of (2), the two displayed coefficient presentations; arbitrary finite bases in place of power bases

proof.text: For S a subfield of K containing K^p, let W be the S-span of the b_i in L. The previous expansion, applied to 1 and b_i b_j in L^p, shows that W contains 1 and is closed under multiplication. It contains the image of S and L^p. It is finite-dimensional over S because it is spanned by the n elements b_i. For nonzero w in W, multiplication by w is an injective S-linear map W to W. Its image has the same dimension as W: map a basis by this injection to an independent family of dim W elements, which is a basis. Thus multiplication is surjective, so some z in W satisfies wz=1. Consequently W is a subfield. Every subfield containing L^p and S contains b_i and their S-linear combinations, while W contains the generators; hence W is their subfield closure.

lean.statement: theorem frobenius_basis_compositum (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (K : Type u) [Field K] [CharP K p] (L : Type v) [Field L] [CharP L p] [Algebra K L] {n : ℕ} (e : Module.Basis (Fin n) K L) (S : Subfield K) (hS : Set.range (fun y : K ↦ y ^ p) ⊆ (S : Set K)) (x : L) : x ∈ Subfield.closure (Set.range (fun y : L ↦ y ^ p) ∪ algebraMap K L '' (S : Set K)) ↔ ∃ c : Fin n → K, (∀ i, c i ∈ S) ∧ x = ∑ i, algebraMap K L (c i) * (e i) ^ p
